title: A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines

learn.hook: With just a compass and a ruler, you can draw a perfect triangle with all sides equal — no measuring angles!
points: Three points NOT on one straight line can be joined to form a triangle: 3 vertices, 3 sides and 3 angles.
Three points on one straight line (collinear points) only give a line segment, not a triangle.
Every point on a circle is the same distance — the radius — from the centre.
Equilateral triangle of side 5 cm: draw AB = 5 cm, open the compass to 5 cm, draw arcs from A and from B; they cross at C.
If O is the centre and A, B are on the circle (not on one diameter), OA = OB, so triangle OAB is isosceles.

example.q: Construct an equilateral triangle with side 4 cm.
steps: Draw an arc from A and another from B
They cross at C; join AC and BC

learn.reallife: Rangoli and kolam artists use circles and equal distances to make beautiful triangle patterns.

games.title: Equilateral construction
items: Draw AB = 4 cm
Open the compass to 4 cm
Draw an arc with centre A
Draw an arc with centre B to cut the first arc at C
Join AC and BC

games.title: Points and circles
items: Three points on one straight line form a triangle
Collinear points only give a line segment.
Every triangle has 3 vertices, 3 sides and 3 angles
That is what 'tri' means: three.
All points on a circle are the same distance from its centre
That distance is the radius.
Joining the centre to two points on a circle (not on one diameter) gives an isosceles triangle
Two sides are radii, so they are equal.
For an equilateral triangle of side 6 cm, set the compass to 3 cm
The compass must open to the full side, 6 cm.

quiz.q: How many vertices, sides and angles does a triangle have?
quiz.explain: A triangle has 3 corners (vertices), 3 sides and 3 angles.
quiz.mistake: Counts each side twice

quiz.q: Points P, Q and R lie on one straight line. Can they form a triangle?
options: Yes, if they are far apart
quiz.explain: Points on one straight line can only be joined into a line segment.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any three points make a triangle

quiz.q: A circle has centre O and radius 4 cm. A is a point on the circle. How long is OA?
quiz.explain: Every point on the circle is at the radius distance from the centre.
quiz.mistake: Uses the diameter instead of the radius

quiz.q: O is the centre of a circle of radius 4 cm. A and B are on the circle and AB = 3 cm. What type of triangle is OAB?
quiz.explain: OA = OB = 4 cm (both radii), but AB = 3 cm. Two equal sides: isosceles.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that both OA and OB are radii

quiz.q: O is the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm. A and B are on the circle and AB = 5 cm. What type of triangle is OAB?
quiz.explain: OA = OB = 5 cm (radii) and AB = 5 cm, so all three sides are equal.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice that AB equals the radius

quiz.q: To construct an equilateral triangle of side 6 cm, how wide should the compass be opened?
quiz.explain: Both arcs must be at 6 cm from the ends of the base, so the compass opens to 6 cm.
quiz.mistake: Halves the side length

quiz.q: Two circles of radius 3 cm have centres A and B, with AB = 3 cm. They cross at C. What is the perimeter of triangle ABC?
quiz.explain: AC = 3 cm (radius of circle A), BC = 3 cm (radius of circle B), AB = 3 cm. Perimeter = 9 cm.
quiz.mistake: Counts only two sides

quiz.q: Which three points can be joined to make a triangle?
options: Three points along a straight ruler edge
Three beads on one tight straight string
Three marks on one straight road line
quiz.explain: Three corners of a notebook are not on one straight line.
quiz.mistake: Does not check whether the points are collinear

teach.ask: Gappu wants to draw a triangle with all sides 5 cm but has no protractor. How can a compass help?
teach.praise: Perfect triangle! Gappu didn't even need a protractor.
teach.nudge: From which two points should Gappu draw the arcs, and how wide?

learn.hook: Three sticks can make a triangle... or can they? Try 2 cm, 3 cm and 10 cm and see what happens!
points: A triangle is made by three line segments. It has 3 sides, 3 angles and 3 vertices.
By sides: equilateral (all 3 sides equal), isosceles (2 sides equal), scalene (all sides different).
By angles: acute (all angles less than 90°), right (one angle is 90°), obtuse (one angle more than 90°).
Triangle inequality: any two sides added together must be MORE than the third side.
If the two shorter sides add up to the longest side or less, no triangle can be made.

example.q: Can sticks of 4 cm, 5 cm and 10 cm make a triangle?
steps: The two shorter sticks are 4 cm and 5 cm
9 cm is less than 10 cm, so the two short sticks cannot reach each other

learn.reallife: Bridges, roof frames and the stands of cricket nets use triangles because triangles keep their shape.

games.title: Triangle truths
items: A triangle can have two right angles.
Two right angles already make 180°, leaving nothing for the third angle.
Sticks of 3 cm, 4 cm and 8 cm can form a triangle.
3 + 4 = 7, which is less than 8.
Sticks of 5 cm, 5 cm and 9 cm can form a triangle.
5 + 5 = 10, which is more than 9.
In an obtuse triangle, one angle is more than 90°.
That is what obtuse means.
A scalene triangle has all three sides of different lengths.
No two sides are equal in a scalene triangle.
A right-angled triangle can be equilateral.
An equilateral triangle has all angles 60°, so none of them is 90°.

quiz.q: A triangle has sides 6 cm, 6 cm and 6 cm. What type is it?
quiz.explain: All three sides are equal, so it is equilateral.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names of triangle types

quiz.q: A triangle has angles 90°, 50° and 40°. What type is it?
quiz.explain: One angle is exactly 90°, so it is a right-angled triangle.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the smaller angles and calls it acute

quiz.q: Which set of lengths can form a triangle?
quiz.explain: 4 + 5 = 9, which is more than 7. In the others the two shorter sides add to the longest side or less.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to check that the two shorter sides add up to MORE than the longest

quiz.q: Two sides of a triangle are 5 cm and 8 cm. Which could be the third side?
quiz.explain: The third side must be more than 8 − 5 = 3 cm and less than 8 + 5 = 13 cm. Only 10 cm fits.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the third side can equal the sum or the difference

quiz.q: A triangle has angles 30°, 40° and 110°. What type is it?
quiz.explain: 110° is more than 90°, so the triangle is obtuse.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a triangle is acute if most of its angles are small

quiz.q: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides of 7 cm and a base of 4 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: Perimeter = 7 + 7 + 4 = 18 cm.
quiz.mistake: Counts the equal side only once

quiz.q: Can a triangle have sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 7 cm?
options: No, because 3 + 4 is not more than 7
Yes, any three lengths make a triangle
quiz.explain: The two shorter sides must add to MORE than the longest. 3 + 4 is exactly 7, so the sides lie flat on one straight line.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'equal to' is good enough

quiz.q: Which triangle has exactly two equal sides?
quiz.explain: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides. Equilateral has all three equal; scalene has none.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up isosceles and equilateral

teach.ask: Gappu has sticks of 2 cm, 3 cm and 10 cm, but cannot make a triangle. Why not? What is the rule?
teach.praise: Ohh! 2 + 3 is less than 10, so the short sticks cannot meet. Gappu understands!
teach.nudge: What must be true about the two shorter sides compared to the longest side?

learn.hook: Think of each compass arc as part of a full circle — then you can SEE whether a triangle is possible!
points: In an SSS construction, each arc is part of a circle around one end of the base, with the given side as radius.
If the two radii add up to MORE than the base, the circles cross (above and below the base): a triangle exists.
If they add up to EXACTLY the base, the circles just touch at one point on the base: the 'triangle' is flat — just a line.
If they add up to LESS than the base, the circles miss each other: no triangle.
Quick check: it is enough to test whether the longest side is less than the sum of the other two.

example.q: Can 3 cm, 4 cm and 8 cm make a triangle? What about 4 cm, 5 cm and 9 cm?
steps: 3, 4, 8: longest 8; 3 + 4 = 7 < 8 → the circles miss → no triangle
4, 5, 9: 4 + 5 = 9 → the circles just touch → flat, no triangle

learn.reallife: Before cutting bamboo sticks for a kite frame, a quick 'longest side' check saves you from a frame that won't close.

games.title: Arc truths
items: It is enough to check if the longest side is less than the sum of the other two
The other two checks are then always true.
If two sides add up exactly to the third, we get a thin triangle
We get a flat line, not a triangle.
Arcs drawn from the ends of the base are parts of circles
The compass draws circles around each end.
With 5, 6 and 12 the arcs cross
5 + 6 = 11 < 12, so they miss.
When arcs cross, they can cross at two points, one above and one below the base
Either point gives a triangle.

quiz.q: Base 8 cm. Arcs of 3 cm and 4 cm are drawn from its ends. What happens?
quiz.explain: 3 + 4 = 7 is less than 8, so the circles cannot reach each other.
quiz.mistake: Thinks arcs always meet somewhere

quiz.q: Base 7 cm. Arcs of 3 cm and 4 cm are drawn from its ends. What happens?
options: They touch at one point on the base, so there is no real triangle
quiz.explain: 3 + 4 = 7 exactly, so the circles just touch on the base — a flat shape.
quiz.mistake: Thinks equal sums still give a triangle

quiz.q: Which set of lengths makes a triangle?
quiz.explain: Longest 9; 4 + 6 = 10 > 9 ✓. The others give 10 = 10, 10 < 11 and 8 < 9.
quiz.mistake: Compares the two shortest sides with each other

quiz.q: For sides 7, 10 and 15, which single check is enough to decide if a triangle is possible?
quiz.explain: Only the longest side can fail; the other two checks are always true.
quiz.mistake: Checks a short side instead of the longest

quiz.q: Two sides of a triangle are 6 cm and 9 cm. What is the largest whole-number length the third side can have?
quiz.explain: It must be less than 6 + 9 = 15, so the largest whole number is 14.
quiz.mistake: Allows the third side to equal the sum

quiz.q: Two sides of a triangle are 6 cm and 9 cm. What is the smallest whole-number length the third side can have?
quiz.explain: The longest side 9 must be less than 6 + third side, so the third side is more than 3: the smallest whole number is 4.
quiz.mistake: Allows the third side to equal the difference

quiz.q: Sticks of 5 cm, 5 cm and 10 cm are put together. What happens?
options: They lie flat — the two short sticks exactly cover the long one
quiz.explain: 5 + 5 = 10, so the two short sticks just lie along the long one.
quiz.mistake: Thinks two equal sides always make an isosceles triangle

quiz.q: Two sides of a triangle are 4 cm and 7 cm. How many whole-number lengths are possible for the third side?
quiz.explain: The third side is more than 7 − 4 = 3 and less than 4 + 7 = 11: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 or 10. That is 7 lengths.
quiz.mistake: Includes 3 or 11

teach.ask: Gappu has sticks of 2 cm, 3 cm and 6 cm and can't make a triangle. Explain using circles!
teach.praise: Now Gappu can see it — the circles just can't reach!
teach.nudge: What do 2 cm and 3 cm add up to, compared with 6 cm?

learn.hook: With just a ruler, a compass and three lengths, you can build a perfect triangle — like an architect!
points: SSS: given three sides, draw one side as the base, then draw arcs from both ends with the other two lengths. Where the arcs cross is the third vertex.
SAS: given two sides and the angle between them, draw one side, make the angle with a protractor, and mark the second side along it.
ASA: given two angles and the side between them, draw the side and make both angles at its ends. Where the lines cross is the third vertex.
If the arcs do not meet, the three lengths cannot make a triangle (the triangle inequality fails).
Knowing only the three angles does not fix the size: many triangles of different sizes have the same angles.

example.q: Construct a triangle ABC with AB = 5 cm, BC = 4 cm and CA = 3 cm.
steps: Draw AB = 5 cm with a ruler
Open the compass to 3 cm and draw an arc from A
Open the compass to 4 cm and draw an arc from B
Mark C where the arcs cross and join AC and BC
example.answer: Triangle ABC is constructed (it has a right angle at C)

learn.reallife: Engineers and tailors draw exact shapes using fixed lengths, just like constructing a triangle with a compass.

games.title: SSS construction steps
items: Draw the base AB = 5 cm
Draw an arc of radius 3 cm from A and an arc of radius 4 cm from B
Mark C where the two arcs cross
Join AC and BC to finish the triangle

games.title: Construction check
items: To construct a triangle from its three sides we use a ruler and a compass.
The ruler draws the base and the compass marks the other two lengths.
If the two arcs do not meet, the three lengths cannot form a triangle.
The two shorter sides are too short to reach each other.
With sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 9 cm, the arcs will meet.
3 + 4 = 7 is less than 9, so the arcs never meet.
For SAS, the given angle must be the angle between the two given sides.
That angle fixes how the two sides open up.
Knowing only the three angles fixes the size of a triangle.
Triangles with the same angles can be small or big.

quiz.q: Which tool helps you mark a fixed length from a point by drawing arcs?
quiz.explain: A compass keeps the same opening, so every point on its arc is the same distance from the centre.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the compass and the protractor

quiz.q: In an SSS construction, AB = 6 cm is the base and AC = 5 cm. What should the compass opening be when drawing the arc from A?
quiz.explain: The arc from A marks all points 5 cm from A, because AC = 5 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses the base length for the arc

quiz.q: Which set of lengths can NOT be used to construct a triangle?
quiz.explain: 2 + 3 = 5, which is less than 6, so the arcs would never meet.
quiz.mistake: Does not check the triangle inequality

quiz.q: Riya constructs a triangle with all angles 60° and one side 5 cm. How long are the other two sides?
quiz.explain: A triangle with all angles 60° is equilateral, so all sides are equal: 5 cm each.
quiz.mistake: Does not link equal angles with equal sides

quiz.q: For an SAS construction, which angle must be given?
options: The angle opposite the longest side
The angle between the two given sides
quiz.explain: SAS means Side–Angle–Side: the angle sits between the two sides.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any angle is enough

quiz.q: You know only that all three angles of a triangle are 60°. How many different-sized triangles can you draw?
quiz.explain: Equal angles fix the shape but not the size. Small and big equilateral triangles all have 60° angles.
quiz.mistake: Thinks angles alone fix the triangle

quiz.q: Arjun draws a base of 7 cm and draws arcs of 3 cm from each end. What happens?
options: They meet and make an isosceles triangle
The arcs do not meet, so there is no triangle
They meet exactly on the base
quiz.explain: 3 + 3 = 6 is less than 7, so the arcs are too short to meet.
quiz.mistake: Thinks two equal sides always make an isosceles triangle

quiz.q: Harpreet constructs a right-angled triangle whose two sides next to the right angle are 3 cm and 4 cm. She measures the third side. What does she find?
quiz.explain: The longest side of this right triangle measures 5 cm. (3, 4, 5 is a famous right-triangle set.) It is less than 3 + 4 = 7 cm, as the triangle inequality says.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two sides, forgetting the third side must be less than their sum

teach.ask: Gappu has three lengths: 5 cm, 4 cm and 3 cm. How can he construct the triangle using a ruler and a compass?
teach.praise: Yay! The arcs crossed and Gappu's triangle is perfect!
teach.nudge: After drawing the base, what do you draw from each end, and where is the third corner?

topics.title: Do two angles always give a triangle? Why 180°?

learn.hook: Draw a base and make 90° at both ends. The two lines go up side by side forever — they never meet!
points: In an ASA construction, the lines from the two ends of the base meet only if the two base angles add up to less than 180°.
If they add up to exactly 180°, the lines are parallel (same-side interior angles) and never meet; if more, they spread apart.
Proof of the angle sum: in triangle ABC, draw a line through A parallel to BC.
The two new angles at A are alternate angles, so they equal ∠B and ∠C.
These two angles and ∠A together form a straight angle, so ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°.

example.q: Base angles of 100° and 85° are drawn at the ends of a base. Will the lines meet?

learn.reallife: Builders check angles at both ends of a roof beam — if they don't add to less than 180°, the roof sides will never meet at the top!

games.title: Can the lines meet?
items: Base angles 60° and 70°
Base angles 90° and 90°
Base angles 120° and 50°
Base angles 100° and 85°
Base angles 30° and 149°
Base angles 95° and 95°

games.title: Angle-sum proof
items: Draw triangle ABC
Draw a line through A parallel to BC
Mark the alternate angles at A equal to ∠B and ∠C
See that the three angles at A make a straight line

quiz.q: The base angles of a triangle are 70° and 80°. What is the third angle?
quiz.mistake: Gives the sum of the two angles

quiz.q: You draw angles of 90° at both ends of a base. What happens?
options: The lines are parallel and never meet
quiz.explain: 90° + 90° = 180°, so the two lines are parallel (same-side interior angles add to 180°).
quiz.mistake: Thinks any two angles give a triangle

quiz.q: For an ASA construction to give a triangle, the two given angles must add up to what?
quiz.explain: Only then is there some angle left over (more than 0°) for the third vertex.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the two angles should make 180°

quiz.q: In the proof of the angle-sum property, which line is drawn?
options: A line from a vertex to the middle of the opposite side
A line cutting an angle in half
A line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side
quiz.explain: A line through A parallel to BC creates alternate angles equal to ∠B and ∠C.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the proof line with a median

quiz.q: In the proof, why is the new angle at A equal to ∠B?
options: Alternate angles between parallel lines are equal
quiz.explain: AB is a transversal of the two parallel lines, and the angles are alternate.
quiz.mistake: Uses the wrong angle fact

quiz.q: In the proof, why do the three angles at A add up to 180°?
options: Together they form a straight angle
quiz.explain: The three angles sit side by side on the straight line through A.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the reason is that there are three angles

quiz.q: One base angle is 100°. What is the largest whole-number size the other base angle can be so that a triangle is still possible?
quiz.explain: The two must add to less than 180°, so the other is less than 80°: at most 79°.
quiz.mistake: Allows the angles to add to exactly 180°

quiz.q: Is a triangle with base angles 45° and 134° possible? If yes, what is the third angle?
quiz.explain: 45° + 134° = 179°, which is less than 180°. The third angle is 180° − 179° = 1° — a very thin triangle!
quiz.mistake: Thinks very large angles can never be in a triangle

teach.ask: Gappu drew 100° and 90° at the ends of a base, and the lines never met. Why? And why do triangle angles add to 180°?
teach.praise: Superb proof! Gappu now knows WHY it's 180°.
teach.nudge: What do 100° and 90° add up to?

learn.hook: Tear off the three corners of any paper triangle and put them side by side. They always make a straight line!
points: The three angles of every triangle add up to 180°.
Reason: draw a line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side. The alternate angles copy the two base angles, and together with the top angle they fill a straight angle (180°).
So if we know two angles, the third = 180° − (sum of the two).
Each angle of an equilateral triangle is 180° ÷ 3 = 60°. In a right triangle, the other two angles add up to 90°.
Exterior angle: if one side is extended, the outside angle equals the sum of the two opposite inside angles.

example.q: Two angles of a triangle are 65° and 45°. Find the third angle.

learn.reallife: Carpenters and kite makers use the 180° rule to cut triangular pieces that fit perfectly.

items.q: Each angle of an equilateral triangle
Exterior angle when opposite inside angles are 50° and 60°

quiz.q: Two angles of a triangle are 65° and 45°. What is the third angle?
quiz.mistake: Adds the two angles and stops there

quiz.q: In a right-angled triangle, one of the other angles is 35°. What is the third angle?
quiz.explain: 180° − 90° − 35° = 55°. The two smaller angles of a right triangle add up to 90°.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to subtract the right angle

quiz.q: What is each angle of an equilateral triangle?
quiz.explain: The three angles are equal and add up to 180°. 180° ÷ 3 = 60°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every triangle has a right angle

quiz.q: In an isosceles triangle, the two equal angles are 50° each. What is the third angle?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts only one 50°

quiz.q: The angles of a triangle are x, 2x and 3x. What is x?
quiz.mistake: Divides 180 by 3 because there are three angles

quiz.q: Can a triangle have angles 100°, 50° and 40°?
options: Yes, all angles are less than 180°
No, because they add up to 190°
Yes, it is an obtuse triangle
quiz.explain: 100 + 50 + 40 = 190°, but the angles of a triangle must add up to exactly 180°.
quiz.mistake: Checks each angle alone instead of the total

quiz.q: One side of a triangle is extended. The exterior angle is 120° and one opposite interior angle is 70°. What is the other opposite interior angle?
quiz.explain: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles: 120° − 70° = 50°.
steps: Exterior angle = sum of the two opposite interior angles
quiz.mistake: Subtracts from 180° instead of using the exterior angle rule

quiz.q: Why can't a triangle have two obtuse angles?
options: Obtuse angles cannot be drawn in a triangle
Two obtuse angles already add up to more than 180°
Triangles must have a right angle
quiz.explain: Each obtuse angle is more than 90°, so two of them make more than 180°. Then nothing is left for the third angle.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect angle types to the 180° total

teach.ask: Gappu measured the angles of a triangle and got 70°, 60° and 50°. Is there a rule for the three angles of every triangle?
teach.praise: Amazing! 70 + 60 + 50 = 180. Gappu tore the corners of his paper triangle and checked!
teach.nudge: What do the three angles of any triangle add up to?

learn.hook: Drop a stone on a string from a tree branch — it hangs straight down. An altitude is the triangle's 'straight down' line!
points: An altitude is the perpendicular segment from a vertex to the opposite side (or to that side extended).
To draw it: lay a ruler along the side, slide a set square along the ruler until its upright edge passes through the vertex, and draw.
Every triangle has three altitudes, one from each vertex.
Acute triangle: all three altitudes are inside. Right triangle: the two sides at the right angle are themselves altitudes.
Obtuse triangle: the altitudes from the two acute-angle vertices fall outside, so we extend the opposite sides.

example.q: In right triangle ABC the right angle is at B. What is the altitude from A to BC?
steps: An altitude from A must meet BC at 90°
AB already meets BC at 90° at B

learn.reallife: Architects measure the height of a sloping roof using an altitude — the straight-up distance, not the slanted edge.

games.title: Where does the altitude lie?
items: Any altitude of an acute triangle
Altitude from the obtuse-angle vertex
Altitudes from the two acute vertices of an obtuse triangle
Altitude from the right-angle vertex of a right triangle
Altitudes from the two acute vertices of a right triangle

games.title: Altitude facts
items: Every triangle has three altitudes
One from each vertex.
An altitude meets the opposite side (or its extension) at 90°
That's what perpendicular means.
An altitude always meets the opposite side at its midpoint
That describes a median, not an altitude.
In an obtuse triangle we may need to extend a side to draw an altitude
Two altitudes fall outside.
In an acute triangle, an altitude can lie outside
All three are inside an acute triangle.

quiz.q: What is an altitude of a triangle?
options: A line that cuts an angle in half
A perpendicular segment from a vertex to the opposite side or its extension
A segment from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side
quiz.explain: An altitude goes from a vertex and meets the opposite side's line at 90°.
quiz.mistake: Confuses an altitude with a median

quiz.q: How many altitudes does a triangle have?
quiz.explain: One altitude from each of the 3 vertices.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only the base has an altitude

quiz.q: What angle does an altitude make with the side (or extended side) it meets?
quiz.explain: An altitude is perpendicular to that side.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the angle depends on the triangle

quiz.q: In an obtuse triangle, where do the altitudes from the two acute-angle vertices lie?
quiz.explain: The opposite sides must be extended, and the altitudes meet these extensions outside.
quiz.mistake: Thinks altitudes are always inside

quiz.q: In triangle ABC the right angle is at B. What is the altitude from A to BC?
quiz.explain: AB already meets BC at 90°, so AB is the altitude from A.
quiz.mistake: Picks the longest side AC

quiz.q: Which tools are best for drawing an altitude?
options: A set square and a ruler
quiz.explain: The ruler holds the side's line and the set square gives the 90° edge.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any tool that draws lines will do

quiz.q: Where do all three altitudes of an acute triangle lie?
quiz.explain: Every angle is less than 90°, so each altitude lands inside the opposite side.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up acute and obtuse triangles

quiz.q: From vertex P, Rani draws a segment to the opposite side that meets it at 70°. Is it an altitude?
options: Yes — any segment from a vertex is an altitude
No — altitudes start at the midpoint
No — an altitude must meet the side at 90°
quiz.explain: Only a segment meeting the side at a right angle is an altitude.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any segment from a vertex counts

teach.ask: Gappu has an obtuse triangle and can't find where the altitude from an acute corner should go. Help!
teach.praise: Got it! Gappu extended the side and dropped the perpendicular.
teach.nudge: What should Gappu do to the opposite side first?
